When Athens Paralysed: How the Year's Biggest Traffic Jam Was Created

2026-10-02 Kostas Papadimitriou (4troxoi.gr) TomTom Traffic Index, Athens, traffic congestion, Robbie Williams, Kallimarmaro, concert, demonstration, flooding, Greece, congestion data, urban mobility
Read the source article

Quick summary

Greek automotive outlet 4troxoi analyses how Athens experienced its worst traffic jam of the year on October 2, 2025, using TomTom Traffic Index data showing congestion levels reaching 149%, driven by a Robbie Williams concert, a protest march, and heavy rainfall.

Key takeaways

  • TomTom Traffic Index recorded congestion levels at 149% in Athens on October 2, 2025, the highest of the year, surpassing all previous records
  • During peak hours, drivers needed at least 15 minutes to travel just 2.8 kilometres
  • Three factors converged: a Robbie Williams concert at Kallimarmaro stadium drawing tens of thousands of fans, a pro-Palestine protest march blocking central avenues, and sudden heavy rainfall causing localised flooding
  • Greek police closed major arteries including Vasilissis Sofias Avenue, Panepistimiou, Stadiou, and Vasilissis Amalias for the protest
  • Traffic was displaced to Alexandra Avenue, Michalakopoulou, and Kallirois, which could not handle the overflow volume
  • The article uses TomTom Traffic Index data to quantify the cumulative impact of simultaneous events on urban road networks
